O Children of Israel remember My favour wherewith I favoured you by giving thanks through obedience to Me and that I have preferred you your forefathers above all the worlds of their time;. (Remember My favour), recollect my blessings (wherewith I favoured you) with the scripture, the Messenger and Islam (and how I preferred you to the worlds) sought you in preference to the other peoples of your time. Allah reminds the Children of Israel of the favors that He granted their fathers and grandfathers, how He showed preference to them by sending them Messengers from among them and revealing Books to them, more so than any of the other previous nations.

**Favours given to the forefathers.**

Verse 47 asks the Israelites to call to their minds the blessing of Allah, so that the recognition of the benefits they have received may induce them to be thankful to Allah and thus to obey Him. The verse is addressed to the Jews contemporaneous with the Holy Prophet while the blessing had been received by their forefathers. The point is that when a man receives a special favour, his children and grand children too usually partake of the benefits flowing from it; in this sense, the Jews who are being addressed may be said to have received the blessing themselves. (And (remember) when Musa (Moses) said to his people: "O my people! Remember the favor of Allah to you: when He made Prophets among you, made you kings, honored you above the 'Alamin (nations).")(5:20). O Israelites, remember the sacred and worldly blessings which I gave to you, and that I favoured you over all those of your time in terms of prophethood and power.

**Preferred over the nations, the 'Alamin.**

As for Allah giving preference to the Israelites "over the worlds", the phrase means that they were given preference only in certain matters, or only over a large part of men - for example, over the contemporaries of the earlier Israelites. (And We chose them (the Children of Israel) over the 'Alamin, (nations) with knowledge.)(44:32) and,. (and that I preferred you over the 'Alamin) means, "The kingship, Messengers and Books that were granted to them, instead of granting such to the other kingdoms that existed during their time, for every period there is a nation. " It was also reported that Mujahid, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, Qatadah and Isma'il bin Abi Khalid said similarly.

**The community of Muhammad as the best people.**

The Ummah of Muhammad is Better than the Children of Israel. This is the only way the Ayah can be understood, because this Ummah is better than theirs, as Allah said;. (You are the best of people ever raised up for mankind; you enjoin good and forbid evil, and you believe in Allah. And had the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) believed, it would have been better for them)(3:110). Also, the Musnad and Sunan Collections of Hadith recorded that Mu'awiyah bin Haydah Al-Qushayri said that the Messenger of Allah said,. (You (Muslims) are the seventieth nation, but you are the best and most honored of them according to Allah.)

**Acknowledging the favor, and the danger of self-conceit.**

He called the Muslims from the community of Muḥammad to bear witness to the favor or bounty of God Himself saying Say: 'In the bounty of God and in His mercy in that let them rejoice' [10:58]. What a difference between those who bear witness to the favor or bounty they receive and those who bear witness to the bounty of their Lord Himself! The servant's acknowledgment of the favor granted him implies gratitude but with the danger of self-conceit iʿjāb. But the servant's acknowledgment of the bounty of the Real-the One whose majesty is in His description and His beauty in the worthiness of His attribute-involves praise which leads to [God's] approval ījāb.

48.text:
After reminding the Children of Israel of God's favours, the address turns to a warning, so that encouragement and fear stand side by side. "Guard yourselves against the Day on which no soul will be of help to another" names the Day of Judgment. To guard oneself against it means to protect oneself from its punishment by believing and obeying while there is still time. On that Day no person can carry another's burden or make up for what another has failed to do. A father cannot help his son, nor a son his father, and no one can give some of his good deeds to cover another's missing prayers or fasts. Each person will be taken up with his own case. Then the verse closes three more doors. "No intercession will be accepted" means that no one will be able to plead successfully on behalf of those who disbelieved. Other verses make clear that intercession will be granted, by God's permission, for believers who sinned, so what is denied here is intercession for the disbelievers, for whom no one will be given leave to plead at all. "no ransom taken" means that nothing can be paid to buy release. Even if a disbeliever had the whole earth full of gold, and as much again, it would not be accepted from him. "and no help will be given" closes the last door. No relative, no friend, no person of power, and none of the gods people worshipped beside God, will come to their aid or even feel pity for them. Every means of rescue that works in this world, a companion's effort, a payment, a plea, or force, will be useless there unless faith comes first. For the Children of Israel, who trusted in their descent from prophets, the warning is direct: lineage will not save anyone who rejects the truth. The next verses go on to list the particular favours God gave them, beginning with their rescue from Pharaoh.

**The Day on which no soul will be of help to another.**

After Allah reminded the Children of Israel of the favors that He has granted them, He warned them about the duration of the torment which He will punish them with on the Day of Resurrection. (And fear a Day) meaning, the Day of Resurrection,. (When a person shall not avail another) meaning, on that Day, no person shall be of any help to another. (And no bearer of burdens shall bear another's burden)(35:18) (Every man that Day will have enough to make him careless of others.)(80:37) and,. This indeed should serve as a great warning that both the father and the son will not be of help to each other on that Day. The day referred to in verse 48 is the Day of Judgment. As for no one being able to suffice another on that day, the phrase should be understood in the sense of one man paying the dues on behalf of another man. Let us, for example, suppose that a man is found wanting in the performance of obligatory acts of worship like Salah and Sawm (fasting), and another man should suggest that his own prayers and fasts may be transferred to the account of the former in order to make up the deficiency.

**No intercession will be accepted, and for whom.**

(So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them)(74:48) and described the people of the Fire saying,. (Now we have no intercessors. Nor a close friend (to help us)(26:100-101). As for intercession (shafa- ah) not being accepted, the phrase does not totally deny the possibility of intercession on the Day of Judgment; it only means that if a man does not have 'Iman (faith), no intercession in his favour shall be accepted. For the Holy Qur'an makes it clear in certain other verses that Allah will allow intercession to be made on behalf of some people (53:26, 34:23, 2:55 etc.), and will disallow it in the case of those who do not possess 'Iman (21:28, 20:109). Since there would be no intercession on behalf of the latter, the question of its being accepted does not simply arise. 'Receiving support', in usual terms, means getting oneself released from a difficult situation with the help of a strong and powerful friend or patron. On the basis of verse 48, the Mu'tazilah and some other groups of a more recent origin have denied the possibility of all intercession in favour of Muslims. But, as we have shown above, the negation of intercession applies only to disbelievers and infidels.

**No ransom taken.**

(nor will compensation be taken from him) means, that Allah does not accept the disbelievers to ransom themselves. (Verily, those who disbelieved, and died while they were disbelievers, the (whole) earth full of gold will not be accepted from anyone of them even if they offered it as a ransom)(3:91) Allah stated that if the people do not believe in His Messenger and follow what He sent him with, then when they meet Him on the Day of Resurrection, after remaining on the path of disbelief, their family lineage and/or the intercession of their masters will not help them at all. It will not be accepted of them, even if they paid the earth's fill of gold as ransom. Ransom, of course, means the money paid for securing the release of a criminal - this too shall be out of the question.

**No help will be given.**

(nor will they be helped.) means, "no person shall get angry - or anxious - on their behalf and offer them any help, or try to save them from Allah's punishment. " As stated earlier on that Day, neither the relative, nor persons of authority will feel pity for the disbelievers, nor will any ransom be accepted for them. Consequently, they will receive no help from others and they will be helpless themsleves. (nor will they be helped.) meaning, on that Day, they shall neither be helped by any helper, nor shall anyone intercede on their behalf. No repeal or ransom will be accepted for them, all courtesy towards them will have ceased, along with any helpful intercession. The judgment will, on that Day, be up to the Most Great, the Most Just, against whom no intercessor or helper can ever assist. Without appeal, ransom or helper, to where will they turn? In short, none of the ways of receiving help possible in this world will be effective in the other world unless one possesses 'Iman .

**Intercession only by permission.**

On the Day of the Resurrection no intercession will be heard except for the one whom the Real has commanded to intercede for Him. He has permitted it and He in actuality is the greatest intercessor even though the term intercessor is not applied to Him because it is without [divine] instruction tawqīf.133 It is said about it: The intercession of intercessors will not benefit those who have been hit by the calamity of fate. There will be no helpers for them nor ransom accepted from them even if they had the fill of the heavens and earths. (And guard yourselves against a day), and if you do not believe and repent of Judaism, then fear the torment of a day (when no soul will in anything avail another), no unbelieving soul will avail another unbelieving soul, (nor will intercession be accepted from it) and no intercessor will be allowed to intercede, (nor will compensation be received from it) and no ransom accepted, (neither will they be helped) to avoid Allah's chastisement.

49.text:
The account of the favours begins here, and it opens on the worst of them before it turns to the good. "Remember how We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh" is put as a reminder rather than as something new, and the address runs to those living at the time of the Prophet, since the deliverance belongs to their forefathers and the grace is being remembered so that they might believe. The wording keeps the saving first, so the saving is what the verse is about and the torment that follows is only what the saving was from. "who afflicted you with dreadful torment" then gives that torment its description, and the clause carries the torment as something they were made to taste, of the worst kind, not as one act, so it covers a long oppression and not a single injury. "slaughtering your sons and keeping your women" gives the torment its two parts, the male children killed as soon as they were born and the females left living, and behind both there is a prediction, that a child born among the Israelites would bring the rule of Pharaoh to an end, which is why the sons were slaughtered and the females spared, since there was nothing to fear from them and they could serve as maid-servants when they grow up. "That was a severe test from your Lord" closes the verse on the meaning of the whole of it, and the test is taken both as a calamity and as a blessing, because the slaughter is a calamity and it is patience that is tested in a calamity, while the deliverance is a blessing and it is thankfulness that is tested when a blessing comes. What is being remembered is therefore not one favour but two, the injury endured and the saving from it, and the verse after this gives the details of the deliverance itself, the sea separated and Pharaoh's people drowned, so the account that begins here runs on into the next verse.

**Delivered from the people of Pharaoh.**

Now, with Verse 49 begins the account of these favours. The next verse gives us the details about this deliverance. And remember when We delivered you your forefathers the address here and henceforth directed to those living at the time of the our Prophet is about how God blessed their forefathers and is intended to remind them of God’s grace so that they might believe; from the folk of Pharaoh who were visiting you with that is making you taste evil chastisement of the worst kind the sentence here is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person of the pronoun suffixed in najjaynākum ‘We delivered you’; slaughtering your newly-born sons this is explaining what has just been said; and sparing retaining your women doing so because of the saying of some of their priests that a child born among the Israelites shall bring about the end of your rule Pharaoh; and for you therein chastisement or deliverance was a tremendous trial a test or a grace from your Lord. (And (remember) when We delivered you from Fir'awn's (Pharaoh) people, who were afflicting you with a horrible torment,) meaning, 'I - Allah - saved you from them and delivered you from their hands in the company of Musa, after they subjected you to horrible torture.' This favor came after the cursed Pharaoh had a dream in which he saw a fire emerge from Bayt Al-Maqdis (Bayt al-Maqdis), and then the fire entered the houses of the Coptics in Egypt, with the exception of the Children of Israel.

**The torment, and who Pharaoh was.**

It was also said that it means, "They used to exaggerate in tormenting you" according to Al-Qurtubi. We should state here that 'Pharaoh' (Fir'awn) is a title that was given to every disbelieving king who ruled Egypt, whether from the 'Amaliq (Canaanites) or otherwise, just as Caesar (Qaysar) is the title of the disbelieving kings who ruled Rome and Damascus.

**The sons slaughtered and the women spared.**

Someone had made a prediction to the Pharaoh that a child was going to be born among the Israelites who would destroy his kingship. So, he began slaughtering all the male infants as soon as they were born. So, even this leniency was motivated by self-interest. But he would spare the females, as there was nothing to fear from them, and, moreover, they could, on growing up, serve as maid-servants. (slaying your sons) in their tender years (and sparing), using (your women) who were of age: Remember when Allah saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who were tormenting you, slaughtering your sons so you would not survive, and letting your women live so they could serve them, taking great pains to humiliate and insult you.

**A tremendous trial from your Lord.**

(That was a tremendous trial from your Lord), a tremendous calamity from your Lord; and it is also said this means: a tremendous blessing. And for you therein was a tremendous trial from your Lord: It is said that [it was] a great blessing niʿmatun ʿaẓīma and a severe trial miḥnatun shadīda. Ibn Jarir commented that this part of the Ayah means, "Our saving your fathers from the torment that they suffered by the hand of Pharaoh, is a great blessing from your Lord.

**The calamity, and the blessing in it.**

What the verse refers to as "a great trial" is either the slaughter of the sons - which was a calamity, and it is the quality of patience that is tested in a calamity - or the deliverance from the people of the Pharaoh - which was a blessing, and it is the quality of thankfulness which is tested when one receives a blessing. In truth what [came] from God was externally a trial miḥna but it was really for the one who recognized it a blessing niʿma and a kindness minna. The children of Israel were patient in enduring injury from Pharaoh and his people so He appointed prophets from among them and made them kings. " We should mention that in the blessing there a is test, the same as with hardship, for Allah said,.

**Chosen people, and what is asked of them.**

He selected them for a special task: they were to receive God’s scriptures and pass His commandments on to the rest of mankind. This misled later generations of Jews into thinking that they were God’s chosen people, and were assured of salvation in the next world. But such matters as salvation are not a hereditary right of any group. On the Day of Judgement people will be judged individually, according to their actions. To think that anything other than good deeds will avail one, is to underestimate the rigours of that Day. When you were saved from the oppression of Pharaoh and his people, it was a great test for you from your Lord, to see if you would be thankful.

50.text:
The verse before this named the torment and the slaughter, and this one remembers the end of both, so the favour named here is the first of the favours in this passage that is a rescue rather than a sparing. "And remember when We parted the sea, rescued you" puts the parting and the rescue in one clause, and the sea is divided in two for them and on account of them, so that they were able to cross it and escape from their enemy, with the rescue named as a saving from drowning and not as the crossing alone. "and drowned Pharaoh's people before your very eyes" then gives the other part of the same saving, the army that followed them into the sea, and the water gathered back on those who went in after them. What matters most is the last clause, since the drowning is placed in their sight, they were looking at them, and what is remembered is a thing seen and not a thing heard about only. The order of the verse is the order of the escape, the pursuit behind them, and the watching that closed the rescue for those who saw it.

**Divided for you, and a dry path through the sea.**

And remember when We divided split in two for you on account of you the sea such that you were able to cross it and escape from your enemy; and We delivered you from drowning and drowned Pharaoh’s folk his people with him while you were beholding the sea crashing down on top of them. When We divided for you the sea and We delivered you and drowned Pharaoh's folk while you were beholding. Remember Allah’s favour in saving you when He parted the sea and made it a dry path for you to go through, while drowning your enemies, Pharaoh and his followers, before your very eyes, as you looked on. Verse 50 speaks of the splitting of the sea, and clearly proves that miracles do occur at the hands of prophets, which some Westernized Muslims have been trying to deny.

**The pursuit, and the escape.**

He, in his capacity as a messenger of Allah, continued efforts for a long time to make the Pharaoh and his people see Truth, but when they persisted in their denial, Allah commanded him to take the Israelites along with him and leave Egypt surreptitiously. On their way, they came across a sea while the Pharaoh was behind him with his army in hot pursuit. Allah commanded the sea to split, and make way for Sayyidna Musa and his people. (And (remember) when We separated the sea for you and saved you and drowned Fir'awn's (Pharaoh) people while you were watching) means, 'After We saved you from Fir'awn and you escaped with Musa; Fir'awn went out in your pursuit and We parted the sea for you.' Allah mentioned this story in detail, as we will come to know, Allah willing.

**Drowned before your very eyes.**

But when the Pharaoh and his army followed them into the sea, it gathered the water back so that the Pharaoh and his men were drowned then and there. Then Allah mentioned the favour of saving them from drowning and the drowning of Pharaoh and his folk, saying (And when We brought you through) split (the sea and rescued you) from drowning,(and drowned the folk of Pharaoh) and his folk (in your sight) while you were looking at them, three days later.

**They saw the signs and doubted.**

When [the children of Israel] saw these manifest signs in the splitting of the sea and the drowning of the people of Pharaoh they were seized with doubt and said They did not drown even though they were cast into the sea but the children of Israel did see them drowning. What a difference [there is] between one who sees with his own eyes yet doubts and one who only hears [about something] and yet sees it like an eyewitness because of the power of his belief! On the other hand in this community because of their being foremost in their belief in the Messenger of God and because of the power of their perceptive faculties one youth said It is as if I was with the people of the garden exchanging visits and as if I was with the people of the fire clamoring to one another and as if I saw the throne of my Lord in plain sight.

**Relief to their hearts, and the blessings granted.**

(And saved you) meaning, "We saved you from them, drowning them while you watched, bringing relief to your hearts and humiliation to your enemy." In relation to this office, they were granted many other blessings and facilities: victory over their enemies, forgiveness of their sins, special help in times of peril, divine provision for their physical needs, and so on. He selected them for a special task: they were to receive God’s scriptures and pass His commandments on to the rest of mankind. This misled later generations of Jews into thinking that they were God’s chosen people, and were assured of salvation in the next world. But such matters as salvation are not a hereditary right of any group.

51.text:
The verse puts a blessing and a failure in one clause, and the failure is what the blessing is remembered against. "And remember when We appointed forty nights for Moses" is the appointment itself, a set number of nights at the end of which the Torah was to be given to him for them to implement, and the forty is made up of thirty nights with ten more added to the period, so that the fasting was completed and the odour lost by breaking the fast was regained. The appointment is a blessing before it is a temptation, since the scripture and the criterion come out of it, and the nights are named rather than the days. "then you worshipped the calf in his absence, acting wrongfully" is the turn, and it comes in the same clause as the blessing, with no verse between them. The calf is the one that was fashioned for them, a figure made out of gold or silver, and the worship is directed to it after he departed for the appointment, so the absence in this clause is the absence of the forty nights, when he had gone from them to the mountain. The last phrase carries the wrong in the act, and acting wrongfully is taken to mean that the worship was directed to the wrong place, since injustice lies in putting things in the improper places, and the wrong is in the direction of the worship and not only in the calf being taken as a god. The verse after this turns to what comes after the act, so the two stand as the sin and what follows it, and the community he had entrusted to his brother is where the temptation came.

**Forty nights appointed for Moses.**

And when We appointed for wā‘adnā or wa‘adnā Moses forty nights at the end of which We shall give him the Torah for you to implement then you took to yourselves the calf the one which the Samaritan fashioned for you as a god after him that is after he departed for Our appointment and you were evildoers for taking it in worship because you directed your worship to the wrong place. (And when We appointed for Moses forty nights) by giving him the scripture, (and then you chose the calf), you worshipped the calf, (when he had gone from you) to the mountain, (and you were wrong-doers) harmful both to yourselves and others. These forty days were mentioned in Surat Al-A'raf, when Allah said,. (And We appointed for Musa thirty nights and added (to the period) ten (more)(7:142). It was said that these days were during the month of Dhul-Qa'dah plus the first ten days in Dhul-Hijjah, after the Children of Israel were delivered from Fir'awn and they safely crossed the sea. When the Pharaoh had been drowned, the Israelites, according to one report, went back to Egypt, or, according to another, began to live somewhere else. But he was ordered to continue to worship for ten days more, because he had broken his fast after a month and thus lost the special odour which rises from the mouth of a fasting person and which is very pleasant to Allah; so Allah commanded him to fast for ten additional days and regain that odour. Thus, Sayyidna Musa completed forty days of total fasting and devotion.

**The Scripture, the Torah, and the criterion.**

(And (remember) when We gave Musa the Scripture) means, the Tawrah,. (And the criterion) that is that which differentiates between truth and falsehood, guidance and deviation. (So that you may be guided aright), after escaping the sea, as another Ayah in Surat Al-A'raf clearly stated,. (And indeed We gave Musa after We had destroyed the generations of old the Scripture (the Tawrah) as an enlightenment for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, that they might remember (or receive admonition)(28:43). He gladly obeyed the Commandment, and was granted the Torah . Also, remember that the forty nights appointed to Moses were from the blessings of Allah, in which the revelation of the Torah, with its light and guidance, was completed. He selected them for a special task: they were to receive God’s scriptures and pass His commandments on to the rest of mankind.

**The calf taken in his absence.**

He fashioned the figure of a calf out of gold or silver, and put into it some of the dust which he had picked up from under the hooves of the horse of Jibra'il (the Archangel Gabriel), at the time when the Pharaoh and his army had been drowned by the Archangel. The ignorant among the Israelites were so impressed that they started worshipping it. When Moses withdrew from the community for forty days they took the calf as their object of worship and were pleased with that. Yet you went and worshipped the calf during that period, which made you into wrongdoers. Allah then said, "Remember My favor on you when I forgave you for worshipping the calf.

**Wrongdoers, and where the injustice lies.**

Verse 51 calls them "unjust" for having committed this sin, for 'injustice' lies in putting things in the improper places, and idolatory is essentially just that. And (remember) when We appointed for Musa (Moses) forty nights, and (in his absence) you took the calf (for worship), and you were Zalimun (polytheists and wrongdoers)Then after that We forgave you so that you might be grateful And (remember) when We gave Musa the Scripture (the Tawrah) and the criterion (of right and wrong) so that you may be guided aright.

**The community entrusted to his brother, and the temptation.**

It is said that Moses entrusted his community to his brother saying Take my place with my people [7:142]. When he returned he found that they had fallen into temptation fitna. They said This is your God and the God of Moses but he has forgotten [20:88]. [On the other hand] the community of Muḥammad the Chosen spent many years with their prophet. Our Prophet relied on God and did not suggest anyone to lead the community. See how the Real attended to the care of [Muḥammad's] community in preserving their monotheism. By my life they may forfeit their [territorial] borders but they will not compromise their declaration of God's unity tawḥīd.

52.text:
The verse is short because the act it comes after is not, and it turns the verse before it round at its end. "Even then We still forgave you so perhaps you would be grateful" is one clause from end to end, and every part of it is doing work. "Even then" and "still" carry the weight of the turn, since the pardon comes after the calf had been worshipped and not before it, and the pardoning here is of the kind that erases the sins rather than leaves them, with those who did it left alone and not exterminated. "We forgave you" is the blessing itself, and it is put without anything named in this verse that had to come first, though the repentance the forgiveness asked for is recounted in the verse that follows. "so perhaps you would be grateful" gives the end the pardon has, and the word used for perhaps is one that carries expectation, which here cannot mean any doubt or misgiving, since what it carries is that when a man receives a pardon the onlookers may expect him to feel grateful. Gratefulness is therefore the thing the pardon is for, and the verse closes the account of the calf by turning it into a favour, which is how the favours in this passage keep coming, each one after a failure and not after good deeds.

**Pardoned after that act of worship, and what the quickness of it shows.**

Then We pardoned you erasing your sins after that act of worship so that you might be thankful for Our favour upon you. (Then, even after that), after you worshipped the calf, (We pardoned you), left you alone and did not exterminate you (in order that ye might give thanks), so that you might give thanks to Us for pardoning you. The children of Israel worshiped the calf so God most high said Then We pardoned you after that. The quickness [with which God] pardoned such a grave sin indicates the lesser weight of those who were pardoned. The words of God most high testify to that [in addressing the wives of the Prophet] Whoever of you commits manifest indecency the chastisement shall be doubled for her [33:30]. To the community [of Muḥammad ] He said and whoever does an atom's weight of evil shall see it [99:8].

**So that you might be thankful, and what that word carries.**

In saying that they were pardoned so that they might learn gratefulness, the present verse employs the Arabic word La lla which indicates expectation. In the present context it does not mean that Allah had or could have any doubt or misgiving about this or any other matter; what the word implies here is just that when a man receives a pardon, the onlookers may expect him to feel grateful. Then We pardoned you after that so that you might be thankful.

**Forgiven, and not taken to account.**

The Israelites were forgiven only when they had offered Taubah (repentance), as recounted in Verse 54. Then Allah forgave you when you asked for forgiveness, and did not take you to account for it, so that you might be thankful to Him, worshipping Him in the best way and doing as He instructed. In relation to this office, they were granted many other blessings and facilities: victory over their enemies, forgiveness of their sins, special help in times of peril, divine provision for their physical needs, and so on.

**The forty days, and when they ended.**

" This happened after Musa went to the meeting place with his Lord at the end of that period which was forty days. It was said that these days were during the month of Dhul-Qa'dah plus the first ten days in Dhul-Hijjah, after the Children of Israel were delivered from Fir'awn and they safely crossed the sea. And (remember) when We appointed for Musa (Moses) forty nights, and (in his absence) you took the calf (for worship), and you were Zalimun (polytheists and wrongdoers)Then after that We forgave you so that you might be grateful And (remember) when We gave Musa the Scripture (the Tawrah) and the criterion (of right and wrong) so that you may be guided aright.

53.text:
After two verses on the forty nights and the calf, this one turns to what came into their hands at the end of it, and it puts that as a favour rather than as a reward. "And remember when We gave Moses the Scripture" recalls the giving rather than the receiving, and the gift is named first, before anything is said about what the people did with it, which is the order this passage keeps, the sin recorded, the pardon after it, and the book given after both. The Scripture is the book itself, the one given to Moses at the end of the forty nights, and the verse describes it only by naming it here, because the description is what the second half of the verse is for. "the standard to distinguish between right and wrong that perhaps you would be rightly guided" then gives that description, and it does three things at once. The word rendered as the standard is the thing that separates one from the other, so what is given is not only a book but a way of telling apart what is true and what is false, and what is allowed and what is not. The separating is not left general, and the end it is for comes in the same breath, that perhaps you would be rightly guided, which puts the guidance as the reason the book was given and not as something the book happens to produce. The word for perhaps is the same one that closed the verse before, where the pardon was given so that they would be grateful, so the two verses end on the same shape, a thing given and then the thing the giving is meant to arrive at. What is remembered here is therefore a favour that follows a failure, and it stands with the favours named earlier in the passage, the deliverance from Pharaoh and the crossing of the sea, since the book arrives after both of them and is given to the same people.

**The Scripture given to Moses.**

The book named first is read by the commentators as a single known thing rather than as a general description. Ibn Kathīr takes the Scripture to mean the Tawrāh, and al-Jalālayn gives the same reading in the same words, the Scripture being the Torah. Maʿārif-ul-Qurʾān states it plainly from the other side, that Torah is the book which was given to Sayyidnā Mūsā, so the name of the book and the name of the one who received it are fixed together before the verse goes on to its second term. Al-Mukhtaṣar places the whole giving where this passage places it, among the blessings of Allah, and it counts the giving of the Torah as a criterion between truth and falsehood, discriminating between guidance and misguidance, so that they might be guided to the truth through it, as one of those blessings rather than as a separate matter. Ibn Kathīr also fixes the moment of the giving, that it happened after Mūsā went to the meeting place with his Lord at the end of that period which was forty days, so the Scripture is not given at a distance from the story just told but at its end. He brings a second verse to describe the same giving, where Allah says that He gave Mūsā, after He had destroyed the generations of old, the Scripture as an enlightenment for mankind, and a guidance and a mercy, that they might remember, which is the fuller description this verse leaves out and then supplies from the second half of its own wording.

**What the standard separates.**

The second term is where the sources spend their attention, and they agree on what it does before they differ on what it is. Maʿārif-ul-Qurʾān gives the word's standing first, that in the language of the Holy Qurʾān al-Furqān is a term signifying something which separates truth from falsehood or distinguishes the one from the other, so the term is not proper to this verse but is used wherever a separation of that kind is meant. Al-Jalālayn reads the standard as an explicative supplement of Torah, that is, the one that discriminates between truth and falsehood and between what is licit and what is illicit, and it ties the term to the root from which it comes, so the separating named here is the act the word itself carries. Ibn Kathīr's gloss is shorter and runs the same way, that the criterion is that which differentiates between truth and falsehood, guidance and deviation, which puts the second pair beside the first and makes the separation a matter of direction as well as of truth. Tanwīr al-Miqbās gives the separation its content, that Allah showed in it the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions, as well as other things, so the standard is not an idea hovering over the book but the book's own rulings laid out. Al-Mukhtaṣar keeps the same two poles as Ibn Kathīr, guidance and misguidance, and adds that the guidance comes through the book, so the instrument and the way it works are named together.

**Three readings of what the standard is, and how they stand together.**

Maʿārif-ul-Qurʾān sets out the options rather than choosing one, and the way they are set out is what makes the verse difficult. It refers either to the injunctions of the Sharīʿah which are to be found in the Torah, for the Sharīʿah resolves all the differences that may arise with regard to the doctrines or the practice of good deeds, or to miracles which decide between a true or a false claim in a palpable manner, or even to the Torah itself, which has the twin qualities of being a Book of Allah and of being an instrument for separating truth from falsehood. The first and the third are not rivals, since one names the book and the other names what is in it, and the glosses that stay close to the wording, the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions, are the first reading spelled out. The second is different in kind, because a miracle separates a true claim from a false one at the moment it happens and leaves nothing behind to be consulted, while the book separates them afterwards and for anyone, which is what the word for perhaps at the end of the verse needs if the guidance is to reach those who were not there. Tanwīr al-Miqbās carries a fourth reading, that it is also said that this means triumph over Pharaoh, and the form in which it is reported marks it as the furthest of the four from the word, since a deliverance is not a standard in the sense the other readings give, though it does decide a claim in fact. Ibn Kathīr stays with truth and falsehood, guidance and deviation, which is the first and the third reading held together, and nothing in the verse's own wording presses beyond that.

**When it was given, and after what.**

The placing of the gift is given in some detail, and the detail matters because it ties the verse to the two before it. Ibn Kathīr records that this happened after Mūsā went to the meeting place with his Lord at the end of that period which was forty days, and that these forty days were mentioned in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, where Allah says that He appointed for Mūsā thirty nights and added to the period ten more. He carries a report on which days they were, that it was said that they were during the month of Dhul-Qaʿdah plus the first ten days in Dhul-Hijjah, after the Children of Israel were delivered from Firʿawn and they safely crossed the sea. On the last clause of this verse he adds one further note of time, that the guidance named here comes after escaping the sea, so the book is given to a people who have already been brought out and have already failed once on the way. The order the sources give is therefore a sequence and not a list, the deliverance, the crossing, the forty nights, the calf, the pardon, and then the Scripture, and the verse is placed last in that sequence on purpose, since a book that separates truth from falsehood is what a people need after they have mistaken a calf for a god.

**What being guided comes to.**

The closing clause is read from both of its ends. Al-Mukhtaṣar takes it as being guided to the truth through the book, al-Jalālayn as being guided by it away from error, and Tanwīr al-Miqbās as being led rightfully, guided to avoid error, so the guidance is described as a movement towards the truth and as a turning away from error at the same time, with the book as the instrument in every one of the three. Tazkīrul Qurʾān, commenting across this passage, describes what the guided life amounts to once the standard is in hand, that true piety is to worship God alone, to believe in Him though one has not seen Him, to live in fear of Judgement Day, to subsist on the pure things of the earth, and to prevent whomsoever one can from falling into sin, and that it is those who adopt this way of life who will be successful in the next world. That is the guidance the verse names, and it is why the giving of the book is counted among the favours rather than among the demands. The verse before this closed on gratitude and this one closes on guidance, and the verse that follows turns to what was asked of the people who had worshipped the calf, the repentance and the execution of the guilty among them, so the standard given here is what the demand there is measured by.

54.text:
The verse before this named the book that was given, and this one goes back to what was asked of the people before it was given to them. "And remember when Moses said to his people" puts the verse as a word to the people, and the people addressed are those who had worshipped the calf, so the word is not to the whole of them but to the part of them that had gone wrong. "O my people" is the call itself, and it is the same call the verse opened with, which is how a word that is meant to be taken is put, since the one who speaks keeps the group he speaks to as his own group. "Surely you have wronged yourselves by worshipping the calf" states the wrong and puts it on them, and the wrong is described as being against themselves rather than against any other, because the taking of the calf for a god harms the one who takes it and does not reach Allah. "so turn in repentance to your Creator and execute the calf-worshippers among yourselves" then gives the two parts of what is asked, the turning and the killing, and the turning is put with the Creator rather than with any other name, which sets the wrong against the making of them. The execution comes in the same clause as the repentance and not after it, and the form it takes is that those who did not worship the calf kill those who did, so the turning is carried out by the people on themselves and not by someone set over them. "That is best for you in the sight of your Creator" is the reason given for a thing asked that would otherwise look too hard, and the good named here is the good of the end rather than of the act, since the killing is not a good in itself but is what the turning required of them. "Then He accepted your repentance" closes the asking with its answer, and the accepting comes after the carrying out and not before it, which is the order the two verses before this had already begun, the sin and then the pardon. "Surely He is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful" ends the verse on the Accepter of Repentance and the Most Merciful rather than on a thing to come, and those two are why the turning asked of them could be carried out at all, since a turning that is accepted has an end it comes to. The verse after this turns from the repentance to the asking to see Allah, and to what came to it.

**Wronged yourselves by worshipping the calf.**

And when Moses said to his people those who worshipped the calf ‘My people you have done wrong against yourselves by your taking the golden calf for a god; now turn to your Creator away from that worship of the calf and slay one another that is let the innocent of you slay the guilty; That slaughter will be better for you in your Creator’s sight’ who made it easier for you to accomplish this and sent down a dark cloud over you so that none of you was able to see the other and show him mercy such that almost seventy thousand of you were killed; and He will turn to you relenting before your turning in repentance; truly He is the Relenting the Merciful. (And when Moses said unto his people: O my people! Ye have wronged yourselves) harmed yourselves (by your choosing of the calf) by worshipping the calf; and when Moses was then asked what to do, he said to them: Also, remember that Allah’s allowing you to ask His forgiveness for worshipping the calf, when Moses ﷺ told you that you had wronged yourselves by taking the calf as a god and worshipping it, were from the blessings of Allah. Allah then mentioned the story of Moses with his people, saying:

**Turn in repentance to your Creator.**

This verse describes the special mode of offering their Taubah (repentance) which was prescribed for the Israelites in this situation, -- that is to say, those who had not indulged in the worship of the golden calf should execute those who had. (to your Bari' (Creator) alerts the Children of Israel to the enormity of their error and means, "Repent to He Who created you after you associated others with Him in worship." (so turn in penitence to your Creator), again they asked him how to turn in penitence to Allah, and he said: Ibn Jarir narrated that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Musa said to his people,.

**Kill each other, the innocent killing the wrongdoers.**

("So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill each other (the innocent kill the wrongdoers among you), that will be better for you with your Creator." Then He accepted your repentance. Truly, He is the One Who accepts repentance, the Most Merciful.) Allah ordered Musa to command his people to kill each other. He ordered those who worshipped the calf to sit down and those who did not worship the calf to stand holding knives in their hands. When they started killing them, a great darkness suddenly overcame them. After the darkness lifted, they had killed seventy thousand of them. Those who were killed among them were forgiven, and those who remained alive were also forgiven." (and kill (the guilty) among yourselves) let those who did not worship the calf kill those who worshipped it. Moses told you to ask for forgiveness and repent to your Creator by some of you killing others, because turning to Him in this way was better for you than persisting in disbelief, which would lead to an eternity in the fire of Hell. Similarly, in the Islamic Shari'ah too, certain major sins necessarily entail capital punishment even when the sinner has offered this Taubah -- for example, life in return for a life in the case of intentional homicide, or death by stoning in the case of adultery established through proper evidence. (That) penitence and killing (will be best for you with your Creator and He will relent towards you) He will forgive you.

**Then He accepted your repentance.**

This was the repentance required from the Children of Israel for worshipping the calf. (And when they regretted and saw that they had gone astray, they (repented and) said: "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us")(7:149). An-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded Ibn 'Abbas saying, "Allah told the Children of Israel that their repentance would be to slay by the sword every person they meet, be he father or son. " This is part of the Hadith about the trials that we will mention in Surat Ta Ha, Allah willing. So, you did this with Allah’s approval, and He forgave you, for He is Forgiving and Merciful with His servants. Then the Israelites acted upon this divine commandments, they became worthy of receiving the mercy and favour of Allah in the other world.

**The worship of the calf, and the sword of struggle.**

"Take care not to suppose that your worship of the calf has harmed the majesty of the Self-Sufficient or that it is a defect for His kingship and lordhood. "Cut off the heads of your souls with the sword of struggle so that you may reach Me. True piety is to worship God alone, to believe in Him though one has not seen Him, to live in fear of Judgement Day, to subsist on the pure things of the earth, to prevent whomsoever one can from falling into sin. It is those who adopt this way of life who will be successful in the next world.

**What Moses fancied of himself at the mountain.**

Sahl ʿAbdallāh Tustarī said, "God spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai, and the exaltedness of the Lord God's speech made that mountain like carnelian. Moses' turned his gaze to himself: 'Who is like me? For the God of the world and the world's folk is talking to me without intermediary, and my standing place has turned into carnelian!' "God did not let that pass. What do you see?' "Moses looked around and saw a thousand mountains of carnelian like Mount Sinai, on each mountain a man in the form of Moses, wearing a blanket like him, a hat on his head, a staff in hand, and talking to the Lord of the universe. " The tongue of Moses' state was saying, "I fancied that you were one body with me. If You do not approve of me as a lover, approve of me as Your servant. If I am not worthy of servanthood, accept me for doghood, so that I may be the dog of Your threshold.

55.text:
The verses before this have been about what was given, and this one is the first that is an asking and what came to it. "And remember when you said, O Moses" puts the people speaking to the one sent to them in their own words, and the saying is what the verse is about, since the answer comes at the end and not at the start. "We will never believe you until we see Allah with our own eyes" is the thing they set, and the wording keeps the belief and the seeing together, so what is being asked for is not another sign but sight of Allah Himself, with their own eyes, and not the hearing of a word they could not be sure of. The clause puts the belief behind the seeing, so what they undertake is that they will not believe until the seeing comes, and the seeing named is put as the one thing that would end that. "so a thunderbolt struck you while you were looking on" is the answer, and it arrives in the same verse as the asking rather than in a verse after it, which is what makes the sequence so short. The thunderbolt is described as a shout and as a fire, and it took them while they were watching, so the seeing they asked for is what they got, and the last clause puts the striking in front of them rather than away from them, with some of them struck and the rest looking on at what was happening to the others. The verse after this is the raising of them after their death, so the two stand as an asking and its answer, and then a life given back so that the answer could be carried.

**We will never believe you until we see Allah.**

And when you said having gone out with Moses to apologise before God for your worship of the calf and having heard what he had said to you; ‘O Moses we will not believe you till we see God openly’ with our own eyes; and the thunderbolt the shout took you and you died while you were beholding what was happening to you. (And (remember) when you said: "O Musa ! We shall never believe in you until we see Allah plainly.") means, "Publicly", "So that we gaze at Allah. Also, remember when you shamelessly addressed Moses ﷺ, saying that you would not believe him until you saw Allah with your own eyes, in the open before you, and the lightning struck you and killed you, whilst some of you looked at the others. But they promised that they would be finally convinced if they could see Allah with their own eyes.

**The Tablets brought from the mountain.**

Then Sayyidna Musa (Moses) brought the Torah from Mount Tur (Sinai) and presented it to the Israelites as the book of Allah, some of them were insolent enough to say that they could not believe it until and unless Allah Himself told them in so many words. With the permission of Allah, Sayyidna Musa replied that even this condition would be fulfilled, if they went with him to Mount Tur . It was not enough, they said, to hear the speech, for they could not be sure whether it was Allah Himself who had spoken to them or someone else. Arriving there, they heard the words of Allah with their own ears. He said to them, 'These Tablets have Allah's Book, containing what He commanded you and what He forbade for you.' They said, 'Should we believe this statement because you said it? By Allah, we will not believe until we see Allah in the open, until He shows us Himself and says:

**A thunderbolt struck you while you were looking on.**

(We shall never believe in you until we see Allah plainly) and said, "So Allah's wrath fell upon them, a thunderbolt struck them, and they all died. (While you were looking) means, "Some of them were struck with lightning while others were watching. " Allah resurrected those, and struck the others with lightning. " But you were seized with a bolt of lightning while you were looking Then We raised you up after your death, so that you might be grateful. Surely when they spoke from ignorance without any sense whatsoever of shame the convulsion and the thunderbolt blast overtook them.

**They died, and were brought back to life.**

(But you were seized with a bolt of lightning) saying; "They died, and Musa stood up crying and supplicating to Allah, 'O Lord! (If it had been Your will, You could have destroyed them and me before; would You destroy us for the deeds of the foolish ones among us)' Allah revealed to Musa that these seventy men were among those who worshipped the calf. Afterwards, Allah brought them back to life one man at a time, while the rest of them were watching how Allah was bringing them back to life. (Then We raised you up after your death, so that you might be grateful), and said, "Musa said to them, 'Take the Book of Allah.' They said, 'No.' He said, 'What is the matter with you' They said, 'The problem is that we died and came back to life.' He said, 'Take the Book of Allah.' They said, 'No.' So Allah sent some angels who made the mountain topple over them." This shows that the Children of Israel were required to fulfill the commandments after they were brought back to life.

**Compelled to believe, and the commandments still to fulfill.**

The first opinion is that since the Children of Israel witnessed these miracles, they were compelled to believe, so they did not have to fulfill the commandments. Al-Qurtubi said that this is what is correct, because, he said, although the Children of Israel witnessed these tremendous calamities and incidents, that did not mean that they were not responsible for fulfilling the commandments any more. Demanding to see the Essence without divine blessing is an open act of sacrilege which is one of the signs of distance and misery whereas attest ing to the attribute of [divine] governance in the unveilings of might as linked to the kindnesses of nearness is one of the marks of communion and the tokens of felicity. True piety is to worship God alone, to believe in Him though one has not seen Him, to live in fear of Judgement Day, to subsist on the pure things of the earth, to prevent whomsoever one can from falling into sin. It is those who adopt this way of life who will be successful in the next world.

56.text:
The verse before ended on the thunderbolt and on the looking at it, and this one begins where that ended, with the same people alive again. "Then We brought you back to life after your death" takes up the death the last verse named and turns it round in the same clause, and the word for what happened is a raising and a bringing back rather than a new making, since the people raised are the people who fell. The death is stated plainly and not made less, and the return to life is put after it in the order of the verse, so what is remembered here is a life that comes after a death they had brought on themselves, and the two are held together in one clause. "so that perhaps you would be grateful" gives the reason the life was given back, and the being thankful is put as the end of the raising rather than as a thing they had to do first, which is the same shape the pardons in this passage keep having. The word for perhaps carries the same looking for that it carried at the end of the two verses before, where the pardon was for being thankful and the turning was for the sake of what is best, and here the life given back is for being thankful again. The verse is short because it has one thing to say, that the death was not the end of it, and the verses that follow turn to what was given to the same people next, which are the favours this being thankful is asked for.

**Brought back to life after your death, so that you might be thankful.**

Then We raised you up brought you back to life after you were dead so that you might be thankful for this favour of Ours. " But you were seized with a bolt of lightning while you were looking Then We raised you up after your death, so that you might be grateful. (Then We revived you) We brought you back to life (after your death) after burning you, (that ye might give thanks) that you might give thanks that I brought you back to life. This verse refers to death, which suggests that the thunderbolt had killed them. Then We raised you up after you were dead so that you might be thankful.

**What Moses feared, and the new life granted.**

Since the Israelites had always been mistrusting Sayyidna Musa he feared that they would suspect him of having taken the men to a solitary place and got them slaughtered. So, he prayed to Allah to save him from such a vile accusation. Allah granted his prayer, and gave those a new life. (If it had been Your will, You could have destroyed them and me before; would You destroy us for the deeds of the foolish ones among us)' Allah revealed to Musa that these seventy men were among those who worshipped the calf. Afterwards, Allah brought them back to life one man at a time, while the rest of them were watching how Allah was bringing them back to life. (Then We raised you up after your death, so that you might be grateful), and said, "Musa said to them, 'Take the Book of Allah.' They said, 'No.' He said, 'What is the matter with you' They said, 'The problem is that we died and came back to life.' He said, 'Take the Book of Allah.' They said, 'No.' So Allah sent some angels who made the mountain topple over them."

**Death as a punishment, and the two opinions on what followed.**

Ar-Rabi' bin Anas said, "Death was their punishment, and they were resurrected after they died so they could finish out their lives. However, Al-Mawardy said that there are two opinions about this matter. The first opinion is that since the Children of Israel witnessed these miracles, they were compelled to believe, so they did not have to fulfill the commandments. The second opinion states that they were required to adhere to the commandments, so that no responsible adult is free of such responsibilities. Al-Qurtubi said that this is what is correct, because, he said, although the Children of Israel witnessed these tremendous calamities and incidents, that did not mean that they were not responsible for fulfilling the commandments any more. He returned them to consciousness after the blows of punishment over whelmed them in order to fulfill the decree for them and to implement [God's] way of pardoning sin. One of the aspects of generosity is to lower the veil over the defects of servants.

57.text:
After the death and the raising of the last two verses, this one goes back to the wilderness and to what was given to the people in it, and it gives three things before it turns on them. "And remember when We shaded you with clouds and sent down to you manna and quails, saying" is the longest clause in the passage so far, and it carries two gifts and the word that came with them. The shading is the first of the two, and it is put as a covering over them in a place where there was no shade between them and the sun, a fine cloud sent for that while they were in the wilderness, so the favour is a thing over their heads and not a thing in their hands. The manna and the quails are the second, and both are described as sent down rather than as found, which is why the wilderness is named as the place they came to, since neither of the two is a food that a desert gives. The word that comes with them is short, and it is an order of allowance that guides to what is good rather than a thing required of them. "Eat from the good things We have provided for you" is that word, and the eating is put without a limit and without a price, with the good things described as provided and therefore already there, so nothing is asked of them but to take what has been given. "The evildoers certainly did not wrong Us" turns the verse round, and the turn is not about the food at all but about what was done with it, since the wrong named here is a wrong against Allah and the verse denies it in the same clause that it names it. "but wronged themselves" gives the other side of the same denial, and the wrong is put on the ones who did it, so the harm is described as coming back to them rather than as reaching the One they turned from. The verse after this goes on to another favour given to the same people, and to what they were told to do with it.

**Shaded with clouds in the wilderness.**

And We made the cloud overshadow you that is We sheltered you with fine clouds from the heat of the sun while you were in the wilderness; and We sent down in them the clouds upon you manna and quails — which are respectively a type of citrus known as turunjabīn and the quail — and We said ‘Eat of the good things We have provided for you’ and do not store any of it away but they were not grateful for this favour and stored the food and so they were deprived of it; And they did not wrong Us in this but themselves they wronged since the evil consequences of this befell them. (And We shaded you with clouds) "This happened when they were in the desert and the clouds shielded them from the sun. In the Hadith about the trials, An-Nasai recorded Ibn Abbas saying, Allah shaded the Children of Israel with clouds during the years of wandering. When they could not bear the scorching sun, Allah sent them the shade of a thin, white cloud.

**Manna sent down, and what it was.**

When they began to starve, Allah blessed them with Mann (manna) and Salwa . Hence it has been designated as mann which signifies "a gift or favour". And sent down on you Al-Manna, The manna used to descend to them to the trees, and they used to eat whatever they wished of it. Also, Qata0dah said, The manna, which was whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, used to rain down on the Children of Israel, just as the snow falls, from dawn until sunrise. " This is the same opinion reported from Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah and Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, may Allah have mercy upon them. The type of manna that we know provides sufficient food when eaten alone, because it is nutritious and sweet. When manna is mixed with water, it becomes a sweet drink. It also changes composition when mixed with other types of food. (The 'Ajwah (pressed, dried date) is from Paradise and it cures poison, Al-Kam'ah (truffles) is a form of manna, and its liquid heals the eye.") At-Tirmidhi is the only one of them who recorded this Hadith.

**Quails, and the birds placed in their hands.**

Then, quails would not flee but come around them, so that they could catch the birds with little effort. I commanded the mist to cast a shadow over them, I com manded the wind to place roasted birds in their hands, I commanded the clouds to rain down manna and honey on them, I commanded the pillar of light to give them brightness on the nights when there was no moon. The two things being unusual, the Holy Qur'an says that Allah made them "descend" for the benefit of the Israelites. But in answer to the prayer of Sayyidna Musa Allah made a miraculous provision for all their needs.

**The wilderness, and the clothes that did not wear out.**

That is why the wilderness is called Tih which signifies 'having lost one's way'. But, on getting up the next morning, they would always find themselves just where they had started from. The Israelites started on the expedition, but, on approaching Syria, when they came to learn about the military strength of the foe, their courage failed them, and they refused to engage themselves in the Jihad. When their clothes began to wear out, Allah showed another miracle - their clothes would neither go dirty nor wear out, while the clothes of the children grew with their growth. "Look at what I did with the Children of Israel, how many blessings I poured down upon them, how much I caressed them in that empty desert! When a child came into existence from its mother in that empty desert, it came into existence with the set of clothes that it needed. Then, as the child grew up, those clothes never became too old for it, nor did they become dirty. In the state of that person's life, the clothes were his ornament, and in the state of his death, his shroud.

**Eat from the good things We have provided.**

(And We caused the white cloud to overshadow you) in the wilderness (and sent down on you honey and quails) also in the wilderness, (Eat of the good things) of the lawful things (wherewith We have provided you) that We have given you and do not keep any provision for future days. Another of Allah’s blessings was that He sent clouds to shade you from the heat of the sun when you were wandering the earth; and He sent down manna, a sweet drink similar to honey, and quails for you, telling you to consume of the good things He had provided you with. (Eat of the good lawful things We have provided for you,)(7:160) this form of command is a simple order of allowance, guiding to what is good.

**They did not wrong Us, but wronged themselves.**

(And they did not wrong Us but they wronged themselves) means, 'We commanded them to eat from what We gave them, and to perform the acts of worship (but they rebelled).' This Ayah is similar to Allah's statement,. Yet they did save food for future days-(They wronged us not) by saving food, (but they did wrong themselves) they harmed themselves. Their ingratitude and disbelief for these blessings did not affect Allah in any way, but they wronged themselves, losing their share from the good they had done and exposing themselves to suffering. But when they disobeyed this commandment, the meat began to rot. This is how they harmed, not Allah, but themselves. What blessing was there that I did not pour down upon them? Yet they did not know My measure, nor did they show gratitude for the blessings. After they had turned away and disobeyed My command, I did not let them go to ruin.

58.text:
The verse before this gave what was sent down to them, and this one gives the city and the way into it, so the favour moves from what was given to what is asked of them at a door. "And remember when We said" opens on a command and not on a gift, and the saying is put first because what follows is a set of things to do rather than a thing to take. "Enter this city and eat freely from wherever you please" gives the first of them, and the entering and the eating are joined in one clause, so the city is described as a place where the eating is free and without a limit, wherever they please and not in one part of it only. The city is named in the verse only as this city, and it is taken as a holy house and as a village, with more than one reading of which it was. "enter the gate with humility, saying, Absolve us" then gives the manner of the entering, and the manner is the point of the verse, since what is asked is not only that they go in but that they go in bowing, at a small door, with a word on their lips. The word they are told to say is an asking to be absolved, and it is put in the same clause as the humility so that the two are one act and not two. "We will forgive your sins and multiply the reward for the good-doers" is the answer to that asking, and it is given before they have done anything, so the word of pardon is put first and the entering second, which is the order this passage keeps. The forgiving is general and the multiplying is for the good-doers, and the two are named together in one clause, with the reward described as increased rather than as earned. The verse after this is what the wrongdoers did with the word they were given, and the punishment sent on them for changing it.

**Enter this city, and which city it was.**

And when We said to them after they came out of the wilderness ‘Enter this city either the Holy House of Bayt al-Maqdis Bayt al-Maqdis or Jericho Arīhā and eat freely therein wherever you will plentifully and without any restrictions and enter it at the gate its gate prostrating bowing and say ‘our request is for an exoneration’ that is ‘That we be exonerated from our transgressions’ and We shall forgive naghfir a variant reading has one of the two passive forms yughfar or tughfar ‘they will be forgiven’ you your transgressions and We shall give more to those who are virtuous’ — through obedience — in terms of reward. Allah admonished the Jews for avoiding Jihad and not entering the holy land as they had been ordered to do when they came from Egypt with Musa. However, some scholars said that the holy land is Jericho, (Ariha') and this opinion was mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd. Remember, from Allah’s blessings upon you, when He told you to enter Bayt al-Maqdis and abundantly consume, with ease, from the good things in it from any place you wanted. On the other hand is the view that the commandment pertains to the city against which the Israelites had been ordered to engage themselves in a Jihad . And when We said Enter this city and eat freely therein wherever you will and enter it at the gate prostrating and say exoneration and We shall forgive you your transgressions and We shall give more to those who are virtuous.

**Eat freely, and the weariness of the same food.**

(And when We said: Go into this township) the village of Jericho (Ariha) (and eat freely of that which is therein) whenever you will, (and enter the gate prostrate, and say: " Repentance ".) i.e. say: According to Shah Abd al-Qadir when the Israelites grew weary of eating the same Mann and Salwa every day and prayed for being granted the kind of food they were used to (2:61), they were commanded to go to a certain city where they could get what they wished for. So, the commandment in the present verse pertains to the mode of entering this city, and lays down the spiritual etiquette for action and speech on this occasion.

**Enter the gate with humility, saying Absolve us.**

(and enter the gate Sujjadan) means, "While bowing". (and enter the gate in prostration) means, "Through a small door while bowing. " Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that they were ordered to prostrate on their faces when they entered the city, but Ar-Razi discounted this explanation. Khasif said that 'Ikrimah said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "The door mentioned here was facing the Qiblah. (enter the gate in prostration (or bowing with humility) but instead, they entered while their heads were raised in defiance. (The Children of Israel were commanded to enter the door while bowing and to say 'Hittah'. Yet, they entered the door on their behinds, distorting the words. They said; 'Habbah (seed), in Sha'rah (a hair).') " Al-Hasan and Qatadah said that it means, "Say, 'Relieve us from our errors." He told you to prostrate in humility to Him when you entered, asking Him to remove your sins, so that He might answer you, and increase those who do good actions, rewarding them in this way.

**We will forgive your sins and multiply the reward.**

The Verse holds out the promise that if the Israelites obeyed the commandment, their errors would be forgiven. The demand was really insolent, but Allah promised that if they showed their obedience by following the new commandment, He would forgive this error too. Anyhow, the promise of pardon was general, and extended to everyone who was ready to obey the new commandment, while a special reward was promised to those who devoted themselves to good deeds sincerely and wholeheartedly. " there is no god save Allah " ; (We will forgive your sins and increase for the right-doers) increase their good deeds. "We may add that 'sincerity' and 'wholeheartedness' are a very weak rendering in English of the essential quality of the text's Muhsinun (rendered here as "those who are good in deeds"). This word comes from Ihsan which signifies "doing a thing beautifully - that is, in the manner that is proper to it. " Beside this lexical meaning, Ihsan has a technical meaning which has been defined in a famous Hadith: : "Offer your prayers as if you can see Him, and if you do not see Him, He is seeing you (in any case).

**The sequence of the events, and the method of the story.**

The discrepancy between the two views, which raises a question about the chronological sequence of the events, should not confuse us as to the nature of the stories narrated in the Holy Qur'an. This is just what the Holy Qur'an does; in fact, this is a quite usual literary method, and the disturbance of the chronological order in the stories narrated by the Holy Qur'an should not raise irrelevant questions in the mind of the reader - after all, in any and every piece of writing, or even speech, it is the intention which governs the ordering of the material. The real intention here is to draw certain conclusions from the stories, and to illustrate or point out certain spiritual principles. The commandment reported in Verse 58 was sent to them through Sayyidna Yusha' (Joshua) who was the prophet among them at the time.

**What came of it, the word changed and the punishment sent.**

(But those who did wrong changed the word from that which had been told to them for another). But those who did wrong changed the word from that which had been told to them for another, so We sent upon the wrongdoers Rijz (a punishment) from the heaven because of their rebellion. Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "Every word in Allah's Book that says Rijz means, 'a punishment.'" Mujahid, Abu Malik, As-Suddi, Al-Hasan and Qatadah were reported to have said that Rijz means 'Torment.' Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Sa'd bin Malik, Usamah bin Zayd and Khuzaymah bin Thabit said that the Messenger of Allah said,. An-Nasa'i recorded this part of it from Abu Hurayrah only, but he has a chain from the Prophet , explaining Allah's statement,. The children of Israel persisted in neglecting that which they were com manded to do to the point that they were entrusted to preserve [their] speech but they altered it and they were commanded [to take] a position of prostration upon entering [the city] but they did not. They exposed themselves to the arrows of the unseen and then were not able to with stand the injury of their strikes lam yuṬīqū l-iṣābata bi-qarʿihā. They were exposed to unexpected punishments and could not hold up to the blows of their impact fa-lam yathbutū ʿinda ṣadamāt waqʿihā. They were given possession of a great city and told to enter it—not in a vainglorious manner—but in humility and repentance; but instead they started rejoicing in their victory. They should have shown their gratitude by remaining obedient to Him, but they did quite the opposite. God bestowed special blessings upon the Israelites.

59.text:
The verse before this ended on the word they were told to say, and this one is what was done with it. "But the wrongdoers changed the words they were commanded to say" opens on the change itself, and the ones who made it are named as wrongdoers before the change is described, so the verse gives the people first and the act second. The change is in the words and not only in the deed, and the words were ones they were commanded to say, which is what makes the change a change of a command rather than of a habit. What they were told to say was a single word, and what they put in its place was another saying, a phrase about a grain in a hair, put in a manner that turned the command into a joke and the bowing into a slide on their behinds. The verse does not give a reason for the change, and it is put as the worst kind of rebellion and disobedience, a turning in the tongue as well as in the body, since the entering and the saying were both asked for and both were altered. "So We sent down a punishment from the heavens upon them for their rebelliousness" is what came to the change, and it comes from above, which is the direction the word they changed was meant to put them in. The punishment is described as sent down and not as sent out, and it is from the heavens, so what came to a word changed on the ground is a thing let down on them from over their heads. The reason given at the end is the rebelliousness, which ties the punishment back to the change of the word rather than to any other failing, and the verse closes on the cause and not on the number it fell on.

**The word changed for another.**

Then the evildoers among them substituted a saying other than that which had been said to them and said instead ‘A grain inside a hair’ and entered the town dragging themselves on their rears; so We sent down upon the evildoers the replacement of the second person of the previous verse with the overt identification in the third person alladhīna zalamū ‘the evildoers’ is intended to emphasise the depravity of their action wrath a punishment of plague from the heaven for their wickedness for deviating from obedience and within a very short period of time just under seventy thousand of them were dead. (But those who did wrong) to themselves, and these are the people who said: �Repentance� (changed the word which had been told them for another word) they disobeyed the command and said �Wheat!�, (and We sent down upon the evil-doers) who changed the word they were ordered to say (wrath) the plague (from Heaven for their evildoing) for changing the commands they were ordered to fulfil. (But those who did wrong changed the word from that which had been told to them for another).

**Hittah, and the grain inside a hair.**

It appears from the present verse that Allah had commanded the Israelites to say this particular word, Hittatun , while offering their Taubah (repentance), and hence changing the ordained word was in itself a sin. They went so far as to distort even the meaning, and drew upon themselves the divine punishment. (The Children of Israel were commanded to enter the door while bowing and to say 'Hittah'. Yet, they entered the door on their behinds, distorting the words. They said; 'Habbah (seed), in Sha'rah (a hair).') They were commanded to enter the city while bowing down, but they entered while sliding on their rear ends and raising their heads! (enter the gate in prostration (or bowing with humility) but instead, they entered while their heads were raised in defiance.

**The words of the prayer, and what may not be changed in them.**

Similar is the case of the Salah: the different things to be recited in them (like Subhanaka Allahumma At-Tahiyyat Qunut) or the glorification of Allah during the Ruku' (bowing down) and the Sajdah (prostration) all these must be said exactly in the words which have been reported in the hadith; substituting other words is not allowed, even if the meaning does not undergo a change. " The prescribed prayer had the word Nabiyy (Prophet), but the man changed it for Rasul (Messenger). As far as prayers are concerned, the words appointed for the purpose by Allah or by the Holy Prophet have a much greater efficacy than any other words can have. (Qurtubi) That is why those who prepare : ta'widh (translated as 'charms' in absence of an exact counterpart) or awdhah, or suggest words to pray are very careful in keeping to the authentically reported words without the slightest change.
