Between the two halves the description has now covered the age, the colour, the work and the body, and there is nothing left to ask about, which is why the answer that comes back is not a question. "Now you have come with the truth" is what the people answer, and the truth they name is not a truth about Allah or about the command but about the description, so the praise in it is for the ending of the asking and not for the thing asked for. The words are the first in the passage that are not a demand, and the first that put an end to anything, and the verse lets them stand without a reply, which is the only answer the people are given. "Yet they still slaughtered it hesitantly" is the last clause and the strangest one, since the hesitation comes after the truth has been arrived at and not before it, so what is described is not a doubt about the description but a reluctance in the doing, and the reluctance is put in the same sentence as the act, so that the act is done and almost not done at once. The verse does not explain the hesitation, and the explanation given with it is that the cow had by then become a thing of price, and that a command which began with any cow had ended with one cow that had to be bought for the weight of its own skin in gold, so the hesitation is the shape a command takes once it has been asked about three times.

**Neither to till the soil nor water the fields, and without blemish.**

He said ‘He says she shall be a cow not broken not subdued for labour that is to plough the earth churning its soil for sowing tuthīr al-ard the clause describes the word dhalūl and constitutes part of the negation; or to water the tillage that is the land prepared for sowing; one safe from faults and the effects of toil; with no blemish of a colour other than her own on her’. ((Moses) answered: Lo! He saith: Surely she is a cow unyoked) unfettered; (she plougheth not the soil) she is not subjugated for the ploughing of the soil (nor watereth the tilth) nor for carrying water to irrigate it; (whole) free from any blemish (and without mark) spots or flecks of white. Then Moses told them that Allah said the cow was not used for ploughing or irrigating the earth; she had no faults, and no marks of a different colour other than her yellow. He said He says she shall be a cow not broken to plow the earth or to water the tillage with no blemish on her. Just as this cow was not to have been broken in for work nor worn out for the purposes of profits there was to be no color in her inconsistent with the overall grandeur of her color. Rather, it is honorable and fair looking. 'Abdur-Razzaq said that Ma'mar said that Qatadah said that,. (sound) means, "The cow does not suffer from any defects. Mujahid also said that the Ayah means the cow is free from defects. Further, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani said that the Ayah means that its legs and body are free of physical defects.

**No mark of others on them, and no desire in them.**

The allusion in this is to the people of divine friendship walāya who do not exert themselves with anyone or anything other [than God] which is to say that they do not seek to obtain anything through secondary causes and who do not rely in their hearts on external appearances and simulacra. They do not trust in their own choices and contrivance. They are not prey to the claims of desire nor game in the claws of the present world. Carnal desires do not rule them and no human authority controls them. They do not strive at all to obtain what they desire and are not concerned with attaining what they wish for. There is no mark of others upon them nor any sign of [their seeking anything through] secondary causes for they are supported by God annihilated from all else nay effaced as God turns them this way and that. Just as their object of worship maʿbūd is God so their only aim maqṣūd is God. Just as their aim maqṣūd is God so what they bear witness to mashhūd is God and what they have found mawjūd is God. Nay they are effaced in God and [only] God remains after them. If you want me to be pleased and you to be pleased and to take the reins of our life together then look at the world through my eyes and listen with my ears and speak with my tongue.

**Now you have come with the truth.**

They said ‘Now you have brought the truth’ that is now you have explained it clearly; they thus sought it out and found it with a boy very dutiful towards his mother and they eventually purchased it for the equivalent of its weight in gold; and so they sacrificed her even though they very nearly did not on account of its excessive cost. (They said: now thou bringest the Truth) now we know the cow's right description. They said Now you have brought the truth ; and so they sacrificed her even though they very nearly did not. They then replied that now he had brought them a detailed description, correctly identifying the cow. They looked for it and bought her in exchange for her weight in gold.

**They sacrificed it, though they almost did not.**

They sacrificed it, after almost not having done it, due to all their arguing and stubbornness. (So they sacrificed her, though almost they did not) i.e. initially; as it is said because the cow was hugely expensive. In a hadīth it is stated that ‘Had they sacrificed any cow it would have sufficed them but they made it difficult for themselves and so God made it difficult for them’. They sought a stratagem for themselves but when their stratagems failed they submitted to the decree and were rid of the difficulties of the demands. If they had done what they were commanded to do [straight away] their misery would not have been doubled. These Verses show how the Israelites were disposed to disobedience, and how this inclination expressed itself in different forms. The Hadith says that if these people had obeyed Allah's commandment without raising so many doubts and asking unnecessary questions, such strict condition would not have been imposed on them, and the sacrifice of any cow whatsoever would have been accepted. (So they slaughtered it though they were near to not doing it) means, "They did not want to slaughter it." Had they slaughtered a cow, any cow, it would have been sufficient for them, as Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ubaydah have said.

72.text:
The passage turns here from a search to a crime, and the turn is put in the opening words. "This is when a man was killed and you disputed who the killer was" puts the killing first and the dispute second, and the dispute is not about whether the man was killed but about who did it, so the verse is dealing with a death that is agreed on and a hand that is not. The people addressed are the ones disputing, and the killing is put among them rather than outside them, which is why the verse does not name a killer of its own and leaves the naming to what comes next. "but Allah revealed what you concealed" is the second half and the turn in it, since the revealing is not a finding out by an enquiry but an uncovering of a thing that was covered on purpose, and the concealment named is the concealment of the people being spoken to. The two halves answer each other, the dispute being the shape the concealment took in public and the revealing being the end of it, and the verse gives no method for the uncovering, which is what the guidance under it takes up.

**A man was killed, and you disputed who the killer was.**

And when you killed a living soul and disputed thereon iddāra’tum the tā’ of the root-form itdāra’tum has been assimilated with the dāl — and God disclosed what you were hiding this is a parenthetical statement; the story begins here with wa-idh qataltum nafsan ‘and when you killed a soul’… and continues in the following. And (remember) when you killed a man and disagreed among yourselves as to the crime. (And disagreed among yourselves as to the crime) means, "Disputed." (And (remember) when you killed a man and disagreed among yourselves as to the crime) means, some of them said, "You killed him," while the others said, "No you killed him. (And (remember) when ye slew a man) 'Amil (and disagreed concerning it) concerning his murder (and Allah brought forth that which ye were hiding) thus demonstrating what you hid with regard to his murder. Allah reminds the Israelites about when they killed one of their own. They accused each other of it, each rejecting the accusation of having killed him, and accusing someone else, until they fought. A murder was committed among the Israelites in Moses’ time.

**Allah revealed what you were hiding.**

But Allah revealed what they were hiding about the murder of the innocent person. (But Allah brought forth that which you were Taktumun) means, "what you were hiding." But Allah brought forth that which you were Taktumun So We said: And when you killed a living soul and disputed thereon-and God disclosed what you were hiding One who is disloyal is afraid and out of fear that his secret will become manifest relies on concealment deception denial and evasion. His fault ʿawāruhu is inevitably discovered his secrets asrāruhu exposed and the coverings astāruhu fall because of the shame of his action. God most high said and God disclosed what you were hiding. But Allah willed that the criminal should be brought to book, and appointed a miraculous way of identifying him -- that is, the dead body of the murdered man should be touched with a part of the flesh of the sacrificial cow.

**The omnipotence of Allah, and the resurrection of the dead man.**

This miraculous event is a manifestation of the omnipotence of Allah, and Holy Qur'an presents it as an argument against those who deny the Resurrection of the dead for the Last Judgment. Verse 73 says that this precedent should induce people to make use of their reason, and see that what has happened in a past instance can as easily happen in a future instance. With regard to this event one may ask as to why Allah made the resurrection of the dead man depend upon his being touched with a part of flesh when he had the power to bring the man back to life without the intervention of any such device; or, one may ask as to why the dead man should have been brought back to life when the name of the murderer could have been revealed even otherwise. In answer to this, we shall say that Allah is omnipotent, and does not act under any kind of compulsion, but that all His actions proceed from His all-embracing wisdom. This long section of the Surah (Chapter) has been dealing with the transgressions of the Israelites, and this is just what the Holy Qur'an intends to bring out in narrating different stories, the narrating of stories not being an object in itself here. The method that God revealed to His prophet to identify the killer was that an animal should be sacrificed, and the dead man’s corpse be struck with a piece of it. The third lesson in this instance was that life after death is no less a reality than life before death. Just as the dead corpse was revived, so every soul will be raised up in the Hereafter and given new life. Instead, Allah made this matter vague, so this is why we should leave it vague.

73.text:
The command that ends the searching is one sentence long. "So We instructed" is put first and on its own, and the instructing is from We and not from Moses, so the round of asking that ran through the last verses closes with a speech that does not come through the prophet at all. "Strike the dead body with a piece of the cow" is the thing instructed, and every part of it is general where the people had been asking for the particular, since the body is the dead body and not a named man, the piece is a piece and not a part with a description, and the cow is the cow they have just bought and not another. The striking is the only act in the passage that anyone is told to do, and it is an act with nothing in it that would produce what follows, which is why the verse does not explain the connection between the blow and the life. The piece is left vague, and the vagueness is kept in what comes with the verse, some of which names a tongue and some a tail, and the point of leaving it vague is that any part of the cow would produce the same thing, so nothing in the miracle depends on the part chosen. "This is how easily Allah brings the dead to life" is the second half, and it turns a single event into a general one, the same words that describe what happened to one body being used for what Allah does with the dead, so the miracle is given as a sign and not as an exception. The body struck is a body that has been dead long enough for the dispute over it to have gone through the people, and the life given back to it is given for a speech and not for a living, since the man names his killer and then dies again, and the second death is what makes the event a sign rather than a rescue. "showing you His signs so that you may understand" names the purpose, and the purpose is not the finding of the killer but the understanding of the people who see it, which puts the reason for the event in the ones who watch it rather than in the one who is raised. What the sign is a sign of is given in the verse itself, the bringing of the dead to life, and the bringing is put in the present and in the general form, so the one body is a case of a rule and not a break in it. The killer is named in what comes with the verse and not in the verse, and the naming is the end of the dispute the last verse described, so the passage runs from a killing that could not be placed to a killing placed by the dead man himself. The order of the telling is worth marking, since the verse puts the striking before the bringing to life, and the bringing to life before the signs, and the signs before the understanding, and the understanding is put last because it is the part that belongs to the people addressed and not to the event.

**Strike the dead body with a piece of the cow.**

so We said ‘Smite him the slain man with part of it’ and so when he was struck with its tongue or its tail he came back to life and said ‘So-and-so killed me’ and after pointing out two of his cousins he died; the two killers were denied the inheritance and were later killed. (So We said: "Strike him (the dead man) with a piece of it (the cow)") meaning, "any part of the cow will produce the miracle (if they struck the dead man with it). (And We said: Smite him) the murdered person (with some of it) with an organ of the cow; and it is also said: with its tail or tongue. Allah told them to hit the murdered man with a piece of the cow which they had been told to sacrifice. God wanted to give life to the dead man so that he could expose his killer through the testimony [of the slain] so He commanded them to kill one of their animals and made it the cause of bringing the slain man to life.

**Thus Allah brings the dead to life, and the murderer is named.**

(Thus Allah brings the dead to life) means, "They struck him with it, and he came back to life. " This Ayah demonstrates Allah's ability in bringing the dead back to life. (Thus) just as He brought 'Amil back to life (Allah bringeth the dead to life) for the Resurrection (and showeth you His portents) bringing the dead to life (so that ye may understand) in order that you may believe in resurrection after death. As this man was brought back to life by Allah, so will He bring the dead back to life on the Day of Judgement. God says even so is the revival for God brings to life the dead and He shows you His signs the proofs of His power so that you might understand that you might reflect and realise that the One capable of reviving a single soul is also capable of reviving a multitude of souls and then believe. He would then bring him to life to tell them who the murderer was. They did this and he told them who had killed him. When this was done, the dead man came back to life, announced the name of his murderer, and died again. Allah made this incident proof against the Jews that the Resurrection shall occur, and ended their disputing and stubbornness over the dead person.

**The allusion in the striking, and the order of the telling.**

The allusion here is to anyone who desires the life of his heart; he will only attain it by sacrificing his lower self since the heart of anyone who sacrifices his lower self through struggle mujāhadāt comes to life by the lights of witnessing mushāhadāt. Likewise when God wants someone's reputation to live forever He causes his reputation in this world to pass into obscurity. This chronological order has not been preserved in the narration, but inverted, and this re-arrangement has a subtle significance. If the chronological order had been kept up, the readers would have supposed that it was only the first of these that was really intended, while the second was added only by way of completing the story.

74.text:
Everything before this verse has been a favour recalled or a command answered, and this one is about what all of it produced. "Even then your hearts became hardened like a rock or even harder" puts the hardening after the things just listed, and the even then is what ties it to them, so the hardening is not a state the people were already in but a state arrived at through the manna and the mountain and the cow and the dead man who spoke. The comparison is to a rock and then past it, and the second half of the comparison is the strange one, since a heart is being measured against a stone and then found worse than the thing it is measured against, which is not a way of putting the heart as very hard but as putting the stone ahead of it, the stone having something the heart has lost. "for some rocks gush rivers; others split, spilling water" is the working out of that, and the two cases given are the two ways a stone can be of use, the water that comes out of it in a river and the water that comes out of it when it breaks, so the verse is not comparing the heart to a stone in general but to a stone that does nothing, and the nothing it does is measured against what stones do. "while others are humbled in awe of Allah" is the third case and the one that goes furthest, since here the stone is given a feeling and a direction, the humbling being an act of the stone and the awe being of Allah, and the heart compared to it has neither. The three cases are put in an order, and the order runs from the stone that gives the most to the stone that gives nothing but itself, and the hearts are placed below all three, so the comparison ends not on a hardness but on a refusal. "And Allah is never unaware of what you do" closes on a different note, and the note is not a threat in words but a statement about knowledge, the doing named being the doing of the people addressed, and the unawareness being denied of Allah rather than affirmed of them, so the last clause leaves the hardening where it is and puts it in front of a knowledge that does not miss it.

**Your hearts became hardened like a rock, or even harder.**

Then your hearts became hardened O you Jews they your hearts became stiffened against acceptance of the truth thereafter that is after what is mentioned of the bringing back to life of the slain man and the other signs before this; and they are like stones in their hardness or even yet harder than these; for there are stones from which rivers come gushing and others split yashshaqqaq the initial tā’ of the root-form yatashaqqaq has been assimilated with the shīn so that water issues from them; and others come down from on high in fear of God while your hearts are unmoved unstirred and not humbled; And God is not heedless of what you do but instead He gives you respite until your time comes ta‘malūna ‘you do’ a variant reading has ya‘malūna ‘they do’ indicating a shift to the third person address. (Then, even after that) after bringing 'Amil back to life and informing you about his murderer, (your hearts were hardened) dry and barren (and became as rocks, or worse than rock, for hardness. For indeed there are rocks from out which rivers gush, and indeed there are some which split asunder so that water floweth from them. And indeed there are some which fall down) from the top of mountains to the bottom (for the fear of Allah) but your hearts are not moved by fear of Allah. Their hearts became hard after these great lessons and incredible miracles, until they became like rocks, and even harder than rocks, because they never changed, whereas rocks change and transform. Then after that your hearts were hardened and became as stones or even worse in hardness. So their hearts were like stones that never become soft. On the contrary, their hearts became all the more hardened against divine guidance. But the hearts of Jews are harder than even these.

**Harder than stone, and the two types of heart.**

Some other scholars said that this Ayah means their hearts are only of two types, as hard as stone or harder than stone. Further, Ibn Jarir commented that this Tafsir means that some of their hearts are as hard as stone and some hearts are harder than stone. This then means that some of them are like the first example, and some others are like the second example. In contrast to them, it has been suggested, the hearts of the Jews are so hard that they are incapable of feeling any sympathy for their fellow-men even in suffering and pain, and hence incapable of wishing to do them good. He made hard stones more excellent than cruel hearts and superior to them. In the case of the ignorant, the hardening of the heart is unkindness, lack of mercy, and distance from the path of the Real. But when the heart is hardened, people begin to manipulate the divine scriptures, for they are used to doing the same with human writings. Such brazenness on their part increases their insensitivity, leading to hardening of their hearts. Their hearts are not moved before the might of their Lord. They remain rigid as the most impervious of rocks. This is why Allah forbade the believers from imitating the Jews when He said,. (Has not the time come for the hearts of those who believe (in the Oneness of Allah Islamic Monotheism) to be affected by Allah's Reminder (this Qur'an), and that which has been revealed of the truth, lest they become as those who received the Scripture (the Tawrah) and the Injil (Gospel) before (i.e. Jews and Christians), and the term was prolonged for them and so their hearts were hardened?

**Some rocks gush rivers, and others split and spill water.**

In contrasting the hearts of the Israelites with stones, the verse refers to three states of the latter: Some stones give forth a great amount of water. The verse places in the highest degree those stones whose affectivity is so strong that rivers gush forth from them, and provide sustenance to beasts and men. Rivers spring from some rocks, and some split, and water comes out of them, gushing and flowing on the earth, benefitting people and animals. Three aspects of the symbolic meaning of rocks have been mentioned in this verse: 1. One sees in the mountains how streams flow over the rocks, finally to join together to form a river. This is symbolic of a certain type of human being: one in whose heart fear of God is lodged, like water in the bosom of a mountain. Some rocks seem to be nothing more than dry boulders; but when cracked, reveal huge pools of water beneath them—wells from which people quench their thirst.

**Others fall down in the fear of Allah, and nothing is hid from Him.**

Still others do not give forth water, but fall down from their place for fear of Allah. The first two of these states are a matter of everyday observation, but the third may be subject to doubt, for the ability to feel fear requires reason and sensibility, and the stones, as one supposes, do not possess these faculties. So, there may be different causes which make stones fall down; some of these causes may be purely physical, while one of them may be the fear of Allah. And some rocks fall from the heights of the mountains in awe of Allah. He is saying, "Water comes from stone, and it becomes soft, and in fear of God it falls into the desert. " The stories say that one of God's prophets was passing through a desert and saw a small stone from which was flowing a great deal of water, much greater than the measure of the stone. Then that shouting and wailing are put aside, and joy and revelry arrive. Whenever he saw that someone was weeping and twisting in himself because of listening to the Qur'an, he would say, "I was like that until the hearts became hardened. But then he is struck by some calamity, which shakes his soul. (Allah is not unaware of) will not leave unpunished (what ye do) of transgressions; and it is said the meaning is: what you hide of transgression. Allah is not unaware of anything we do, but knows everything, and will hold us to account for it.

75.text:
The verse turns from the people of the last verses to the believers who are listening to them. "Do you believers still expect them to be true to you" is a question put to the believers and not to the Jews, and the thing asked about is an expectation, so the verse is dealing with a hope the people addressed have been carrying and not with a command they have been given. The truth named is truth to you, which is a keeping of a word given to the believers rather than a keeping of the law, and the expectation is put as something that has been going on, so the question is asking whether it is to go on. "though a group of them would hear the word of Allah then knowingly corrupt it after understanding it" is the reason the expectation is questioned, and the reason is not that the group has failed to hear but that it heard and then altered what it heard, with the two adverbs doing the work, since knowingly puts the altering in the will and after understanding it puts it after the meaning had been got. The word of Allah named here is a word they had already and not a word being given to them now, and the corruption is of that word, so the verse is not about a people who have not been told but about a people who were told and changed the telling. The group is a group of them and not all of them, which is why the question is about an expectation rather than a judgement, and the answer given is not that the people will not believe but that the believers should not be looking for it in the place they are looking for it. The expectation is therefore not called a mistake but questioned, and the question is answered inside the same sentence by the thing the group did with the word it had heard.

**Do you expect them to be true to you.**

(Have ye any hope that they will be true to you) do you hope, O Muhammad, that the Jews will believe in you (when a party of them) the 70 men who were with Moses (used to listen to the Word of Allah) used to listen to Moses reciting the Word of Allah, (then used to change it) alter it, (after they had understood it) after knowing it and fully understanding it (knowingly?) while knowing that they were altering it? Are you then so eager O believers that they the Jews should believe you seeing there is a party of them a group of their rabbis that heard God’s word in the Torah and then tampered with it changing it and that after they had comprehended it after they had understood it knowingly? knowing full well that they were indulging in mendacity the hamza at the beginning of the verb a-fa-tatma‘ūn is an interrogative for rejection in other words ‘Do not be so eager for they have disbelieved before’. O believers, do not expect, after knowing their true nature and how stubborn they are, that they will be truthful and respond to you. Do you (faithful believers) covet that they will believe in your religion inspite of the fact that a party of them (Jewish rabbis) used to hear the Word of Allah (the Tawrah), then they used to change it knowingly after they understood it And when they (Jews) meet those who believe (Muslims), they say, "We believe," but when they meet one another in private, they say, "Shall you (Jews) tell them (Muslims) what Allah has revealed to you that they (Muslims) may argue with you (Jews) about it before your Lord? The Muslims used to take great pains in trying to make the Jews accept Islam. Having recounted so many stories of the perversity of the Jews, the Holy Qur'an points out to the Muslims that they cannot expect such a people to be sensible, and asks them not to worry much about them.

**A group of them heard the word of Allah and corrupted it.**

The "Word of Allah" mentioned in the verse refers to the Torah which the Jews had "heard" from the prophets, and the distortion pertains to the changes made in the words themselves or in the sense or in both; or it refers to the words of Allah which the seventy men had heard directly on the Mount Tur (Sinai) where they had gone to seek divine confirmation of what Sayyidna Musa (Moses) had been telling and the distortion pertains to their declaration before their people that Allah had promised to forgive them if they could not act upon certain commandments. For, some of the Jews have been committing an even more heinous sin - they used to change and distort the Word of Allah in spite of knowing the ignominy of such a deed. A group of their scholars heard the word of Allah, revealed to them in the Torah, and then changed its words and meanings after they had understood what it really meant; and they did this fully aware of the seriousness of the crime. (Inspite of the fact that a party of them (Jewish rabbis) used to hear the Word of Allah (the Tawrah), then they used to change it) meaning, distort its meaning,. (used to hear the Word of Allah (the Tawrah), then they used to change it) "They altered the Tawrah that Allah revealed to them, making it say that the lawful is unlawful and the prohibited is allowed, and that what is right is false and that what is false is right. So when a person seeking the truth comes to them with a bribe, they judge his case by the Book of Allah, but when a person comes to them seeking to do evil with a bribe, they take out the other (distorted) book, in which it is stated that he is in the right. When someone comes to them who is not seeking what is right, nor offering them bribe, then they enjoin righteousness on him. Why would they believe you when they already heard by means of the messageḍ How can those who do not remain in a state of faith imān after eyewitnessing ʿiyān believe by means of demonstrative proof burhānḍ That which does not hold true for the Real does not hold true for you. How can those who are not ashamed before the Real be ashamed before youḍ.

**The attitude behind the altering.**

One who has such irreverent attitude towards the divine scriptures can never appreciate the gravity of matters concerning God: he hears the word of God, but he can always find words to show that the commandment does not apply to him; he believes in God, but his insensitivity makes him commit acts of flagrant rebellion against Him which no one who really believes that God is watching over him, and hearing what he says, would ever dare to perpetrate. Seeking out loopholes in any part of the Holy scriptures that did not conform to their wishes, they altered the word of God at will; religion was subordinated to their worldly interests. As for the Jews, they had already altered their own scriptures, though they knew them to be the word of God. However true something may be, if one is bent on denial and intentional distortion, one is sure to find some justification or the other for it. Such a perverse attitude finally leads to deliberate misrepresentation of the true word of God. If he were truly a prophet, the Jews would have been the first to believe in him, for their knowledge of what is written in the scriptures is greater than yours. So, the Holy Qur'an wants the Muslims to realize that men who are so enslaved to their desires and so shameless in their pursuit of evil, cannot be expected to listen to anyone. The Jews who were the contemporaries of the Holy Prophet may not have themselves been involved in some of these transgressions, but since they did not abhor the misdeeds of their forefathers, they are to be considered as their counterparts.

**The seventy men who heard, and the verse of stoning.**

This was revealed about the seventy men who were chosen by Moses to go with him to Allah, exalted is He. When they went with him to the tryst and heard Allah's speech, commanding and prohibiting Moses, they returned to their people. As for the true amongst them, they delivered exactly what they had heard. But a group of them said: we heard Allah at the end of His speech say: if you can do these things, then do them; but if you wish, don't do them and there is no harm upon you . But most Qur'anic exegetes are of the opinion that it was revealed about those who had changed the verse of stoning [adulterers who are married] and the description of Muhammad, Allah bless him and give him peace.

76.text:
The verse has two scenes in it, and the second is the one the believers are not in. "When they meet the believers they say, We believe" is the first, and the meeting is put as an occasion rather than a state, so the belief named in it is a thing spoken on meeting and not a thing kept. The word believers is used for the people being spoken to and the word believe is put in their mouths as something spoken to those people, and the two uses of the same root in one clause are what the verse is built on. "But in private they say to each other" opens the second scene, and the private is the same people saying the same kind of thing with the believers gone, so the change is not in what is believed but in who is listening. "Will you disclose to the believers the knowledge Allah has revealed to you" is what is spoken in the second scene, and it is a question about speaking rather than about believing, the disclosure named being a disclosure of knowledge and the knowledge being what Allah has revealed to them and not to the believers, which is why the thing disclosed is worth concealing. "so that they may use it against you before your Lord" gives the reason for the concealment, and the reason is a use the believers would make of it, an argument held up against them in front of the one who gave it, so the knowledge is treated as a thing that can be turned on the people who have it. "Do you not understand?" closes the verse inside the second scene, and the understanding asked for is not understanding of the prophet or of what he brought but of the consequence of the disclosure, so the last words of the verse are the private people correcting each other for having spoken too much in public. The knowledge disclosed is not named in the verse, and the naming of it is left to what comes with the verse, some of which takes it for the description of the prophet in their own book and some for the judgements they had been given, so the concealment is of a thing the believers would have recognised as their own. The two scenes are not put as a contrast between belief and unbelief but between a speech made in front of the believers and the same speech examined among the people who made it, and the examination is about prudence and not about truth, which is what makes the question at the end a question about consequences.

**When they meet the believers, they say we believe.**

And when they the hypocrites from among the Jews meet those who believe they say ‘We believe’ that Muhammad is a prophet and that he is the one of whom we have been given good tidings in our Book; but when they go in private one to another they their leaders the ones not involved in the hypocrisy say to those hypocrites ‘Do you speak to them the believers of what God has disclosed to you that is what He has made known to you of Muhammad’s s description in the Torah so that they may thereby dispute the lām of li-yuhājjūkum ‘that they may dispute with you’ is the lām of ‘becoming’ with you before your Lord? in the Hereafter and hold the proof against you for not following him Muhammad despite your knowledge of his sincerity? (And when they fall with those who believe) Abu Bakr and his companions, (they say: We believe) in your Prophet, and his description and traits are mentioned in our Book. An instance of their inconsistencies and deviousness occurred when some of them met some believers and acknowledged the truth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the correctness of his message, as the Torah witnessed to it. (And when they (Jews) meet those who believe (Muslims), they say, "We believe") "They believe that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, 'But he was only sent for you (Arabs)'" However, when they meet each other they say, "Do not convey the news about this Prophet to the Arabs, because you used to ask Allah to grant you victory over them when he came, but he was sent to them (not to you). Some of the Jews, seeing the growing power of the Muslims in Madīnah and around it, pretended to have accepted Islam. One of the reasons for the promptness with which the people of Madīnah recognized the Prophet Muhammad, and believed in him, was that they had often heard from their Jewish neighbours of the coming of a final prophet. It was only natural that the Muslims, in their turn, should hope that the Jews would unhesitatingly accept the prophethood of Muhammad. How shocked the Muslims were, then, when they found that, contrary to their expectations, the Jews were not ready to accept their invitation to accept Islam.

**Alone with one another, and back among the others.**

But when they met other Jews who openly declared their adherence to Judaism, they would admit that they were only trying to deceive the Muslims, and were otherwise quite loyal to their own faith. On such occasions, those of the other group used to reprimand them for revealing to the Muslims what they themselves were trying to keep concealed, for a knowledge of the relevant verses of the Torah could be very useful for the Muslims in order to defeat the Jews in their argument. (But when they go apart one with another) when these lowly people return to their leaders (they say) the leaders say to the lowly: Then Allah mentioned the hypocrites of the people of the Book, and it is also said that the reference here is to the lowly from among the people of the Book, saying: But when they were alone with one another they blamed each other because of these acknowledgments, saying that the Muslims might use them as proof that they recognised the truth of Muhammad’s prophethood.

**The disclosure, and what it would have cost them.**

In order to assure the Muslims of their sincerity and to win their favour, these hypocrites would now and then disclose to them that the Torah itself had given out the good tidings of the coming of the Holy Prophet and mentioned the Holy Qur'an. Muhammad and his Companions (of that which Allah hath disclosed to you) about that which Allah has shown you regarding the description and traits of Muhammad in your Book (so that they may contend with you) argue against you (before your Lord concerning it? Have ye then no sense?) do you not have any common sense? Do you speak to them of what God has disclosed to you so that they may thereby dispute with you before your Lordḍ Have you no understandingḍ Do they not know that God knows what they keep secret and what they proclaimḍ They encouraged one another among themselves to reject the Real and to hide the situation from the Muslims. Have you no understanding?’ of the fact that they will contend with you if you speak to them in this way? (And what they reveal?) meaning, when they said to the Companions of Muhammad ,. But they did not know that God was informing His Messenger of their secrets and that a light the Real makes manifest cannot be extinguished by the efforts of anyone other than Him. When the tongue agrees but the mind162 objects it only increases separation.

77.text:
The verse is a single question and it is about knowledge. "Do they not know that Allah is aware of what they conceal and what they reveal" is put as a question whose answer is given in its own form, since the interrogative is affirmative and the not in it is not a doubt but a way of putting the knowledge as something they cannot miss. The two things named are the concealed and the revealed, and the pair covers the whole of what a person does, so the awareness of Allah is not put as reaching one of them and not the other but as reaching both at once, which is what makes the concealment of the last verse pointless. The concealment and the revealing are named in that order, and the order matters, since the hidden comes first in the sentence and the open second, so the awareness is turned first on the thing no one else can see and only then on the thing everyone can, which is the reverse of the order a person would take them in. The question is asked of people who have just been described as speaking one way in public and another in private, and it is asked in a form that expects the answer, so the verse is not opening a doubt about their knowledge but closing a way out of it. The verse does not threaten and does not promise, and the whole of its weight is in the word aware, since an awareness that covers the hidden and the open leaves nothing that can be kept from it.

**Do they not know.**

God says Know they not the interrogative is affirmative the inserted wāw of a-wa-lā is to indicate the supplement that God knows what they keep secret and what they proclaim? that is what they hide and what they reveal in this matter and all other matters so that they may desist from these things. Do they not know that God knows what they keep secret and what they announce? He presents His lordhood and kingship to him and says, "Do they not know that God knows what they keep secret and what they announce? (Are they) i.e. these leaders (then unaware that Allah knoweth that which they keep hidden) amongst themselves (and that which they proclaim?) to Muhammad and his Companions. They behave in this pathetic manner as if they are unaware that Allah knows what they hide, in terms of what they say and do, and what they reveal; but He will reveal it and expose them. With every hope of a positive response, it was with sublime feelings that they called on the Jews to join them in their belief in the Prophet.

**The secret and the hidden, and the apparent.**

When the Lord of the Worlds says that He knows the secret cores and is aware of the hidden things, they sweep the dust of the others from their secret cores and give scatteredness no way into their hearts. When He says that He knows the apparent, they bring truthfulness to bear in their outward interaction with God's creatures. This is why the folk of allusion have said that He knows what they keep secret is a command to watchfulness between servant and Lord, and what they announce is a command to truthfulness in interactions and settling accounts with the creatures. In one of God's books has come, "If you do not know that I see you, that is a defect in your faith. If you do know that I see you, why do you make Me the lowliest of gazers upon you?

**The treachery of the eyes, and what the breasts conceal.**

Allah reminds the Jews that He is omniscient, and knows what they try to keep concealed as well as what they say or do openly. "He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal" [40:19]. There are diverse treacheries in the eyes of the lookers, because the travelers are diverse. The treachery of the eyes of the worshipers is that in the dark night, when it is time for whis pering to God, they fall asleep and the intimacy of seclusion is lost to them. The prophet David received the revelation, "O David, he who claims to love Me is a liar if night comes, and he goes to sleep on Me. Does not every lover love to be secluded with his beloved? " God praised Abraham for this attribute when He said, "When night darkened over him" [6:76].

78.text:
The verse divides the people of the last verses into two, and this is the second of them. "And among them are the illiterate who know nothing about the Scripture except lies" sets a group apart by what it does not know, and the not knowing is of the Scripture itself, so the group named is not outside the book but inside it without it, and the one thing it has in place of the book is a lie. The exception is the hinge of the sentence, since except lies turns a statement about ignorance into a statement about what fills the ignorance, and what fills it is not nothing but something taken for the Scripture. "and so they wishfully speculate" is the consequence, and the speculation is named as wishful, so the guessing is not a shortfall of information but a direction of the will, and the two halves of the verse answer each other, the lie being what is taken for the book and the speculation being the taking of it. The word used for this speculation carries a range of meanings in the Qur'an, and the sense it has here is the weakest of them, an opinion with nothing under it.

**The illiterate among them, who know nothing of the Scripture.**

And there are some of them the Jews that are illiterate unlettered not knowing the Scripture the Torah but only desires lies which were handed down to them by their leaders and which they relied upon; and in their rejection of the prophethood of the Prophet and fabrications of other matters they have mere conjectures and no firm knowledge. And there are among them (Jews) 'Ummyyun (unlettered) people, who know not the Book, but they trust upon Amani (false desires) and they but guess Then woe to those who write the book with their own hands and then say, "This is from Allah," to purchase with it a little price! (Among them are unlettered folk who know not the scripture) they do not know how to read or write it (except from hearsay) except the unfounded things they hear. A group of them do not know how to read or write and do not know what is in the Torah or what it says. In this verse the attribute of unletteredness is a censure of the estranged and a mark of their short coming. In the verse where He says, "Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet" [7:157], it is a praise of MuṣṬafā and a mark of his perfection. (Who know not the Book) meaning, are they not aware of what is in it.

**The tales taught to the masses, and what they guess.**

The scholars who taught these tales, attributing them to past saints, became highly regarded for the theories they expounded were designed to win popular support. Such sacred recipes for cheap salvation are very attractive to the masses, for they give credence to the popular notion based on wishful thinking that there is no need to discipline oneself—no need to lead a responsible life; superstitious charms and magical remedies are enough to cure one’s spiritual ills and have one admitted to heaven. (They but guess) their talk is all surmise based on what they heard from their leaders. They have only lies which they heard from some of their leaders, and think it is the Torah revealed by Allah. (But they trust upon Amani) means, "It is just a false statement that they utter with their tongues. " Qatadah, Abu Al-'Aliyah and Ar-Rabi' said that it means, "They have evil false ideas about Allah." Then, the Jewish scholars did not give them correct or proper information about their religion.

**The word they were given, and the context it was used in.**

Some people do not pay any attention to the context in which the word has been used here, and come to the erroneous conclusion that it is not legitimate to accept or follow any view or injunction based on Zann which they always translate as "a fanciful supposition. Let us explain that the Holy Qur'an uses the word Zann in three ways: " This, no doubt, is one of the lexical meanings of the word, but only one. This verse condemns the Jews for having followed this kind of Zann which consists in a fanciful opinion that is not supported by a respectable argument or goes against a valid one. When someone fancies that having the same meaning is to be of the same kind, that is to go by the road of the road less, and it is nothing but rebellion.

**Cheap salvation, and the dream world.**

Facilitation of eternal salvation became for them a lucrative source of worldly income. They were showered with offerings, for they ushered others along the path to a paradise that did not have to be earned; in return they received worldly wealth that they did not have to labour for. They wanted to live in a dream world, thinking that they had no obligations save the perfunctory performance of certain empty rituals, and deluding themselves into believing that they had certain inalienable rights given by God. Such people cannot accept the call of true religion, for truth demolishes all their wishful thinking, and makes them face the stark realities of life. According to Ibn ‘Abbas, Fara’ and Mujahid—some of the most reliable of the Quranic commentators—the word refers to the mythical tales invented by Jewish scholars. So, it would make no difference at all, if the hypocrites tried to conceal their infidelity from the Muslims, or the other group, not to disclose the verses of the Torah which speak of the Holy Prophet . The position of the Folk of the Sunnah in affirming the attributes of the Real was established according to this rule: the agreement of one name with another does not bring about the agreement of meanings. What God said about Himself should be accepted from the eyeteeth and assented to from the depth of the spirit.
